samples.text:
Nowadays, it is very easy to buy things on credit, for example with a credit card or by paying in instalments. However, many people buy products which they cannot really afford, and they get into debt. This essay will discuss the problems this causes and what can be done to prevent it.

The first problem is financial. When people cannot pay back the money, the interest become higher and higher, so the debt grows very fast. Some people have to borrow more money to pay the old debt, and they cannot escape from this situation. The second problem is stress. People who have big debts are always worried about money, and this can affect their health and their sleep. It can also cause arguments in the family, and in some cases couples even get divorce because of money problems. Moreover, if a person does not pay, the bank can take their house or car, and they may lose everything.

There are several ways to prevent this problem. Firstly, schools should teach children how to manage money, for example how to make a budget and how interest work. If young people learn this early, they will make better decisions in the future. Secondly, banks and shops should check carefully if a customer can pay back before they give them credit. The government can make stricter laws about this. Also, people themselves should think carefully before buying something expensive and ask themselves if they really need it.

In conclusion, buying on credit can lead to growing debt, stress and family problems. I believe that financial education, stricter rules for banks and more careful spending can help people to avoid get into debt.
samples.why: Problems and prevention both addressed · relevant ideas with simple explanation · clear paragraphs, basic sequencing · adequate vocabulary with some repetition (problem) · agreement, word-form and verb-pattern errors that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
Credit cards, store finance and buy-now-pay-later schemes have made it easier than ever to purchase goods without having the money upfront. As a result, many people take on debts they are unable to repay. This essay will discuss the problems this creates and suggest some ways of preventing it.

The most immediate problem is financial difficulty for the borrower. High interest rates mean that a relatively small purchase can turn into a much larger debt if repayments are missed, and some people end up taking out new loans simply to cover existing ones. This can damage their credit record, making it harder to rent a flat or obtain a mortgage in the future. Debt also has a serious psychological cost. People struggling with repayments often experience constant anxiety, which can affect their sleep, their work performance and their relationships. Money worries are a common cause for family conflict, and children in these households may also feel the pressure. At a wider level, widespread personal debt can make an economy more vulnerable during a recession.

Preventing this problem requires both education and regulation. Financial literacy should be taught in schools so that young people understand how interest works and learn to budget before they receive their first credit card. Governments should also require lenders to carry out proper checks on whether customers can realistically afford repayments, and to present the total cost of credit clearly rather than hiding it in small print. Buy-now-pay-later services, which are often marketed at young consumers, should be regulated in the same way as other forms of borrowing. Finally, free debt advice services can help people who are already struggling before their situation gets out of control.

In conclusion, buying on credit can lead to spiralling debt, stress and family tension. Better financial education, responsible lending rules and accessible advice could help to prevent these problems.
samples.why: Clear position throughout · financial, psychological and economic problems extended · prevention measures specific and relevant · good collocation (credit record, small print) · one preposition slip.

samples.text:
Access to credit has never been easier. Credit cards, retail finance and instant buy-now-pay-later options allow consumers to acquire goods at the touch of a button, often without fully registering what they will eventually pay. For those who borrow beyond their means, the consequences can be severe, and preventing them requires action from educators, lenders and regulators alike.

The most direct harm is the way debt can escalate. High interest and penalty charges mean that modest purchases can grow into substantial obligations, and borrowers who fall behind may resort to further borrowing to service existing debts, entering a cycle from which escape is difficult. A poor credit history can then restrict access to housing and affordable loans for years. The personal toll extends well beyond finances. Persistent money worries are closely associated with anxiety, sleep problems and depression, and financial strain is a frequent source of tension between partners that affects children as well. On a societal scale, high levels of household debt leave economies more fragile, since heavily indebted consumers cut spending sharply when conditions deteriorate.

Prevention should begin with education. Teaching financial literacy in schools, covering budgeting, compound interest and the true cost of borrowing, equips young people to make informed decisions before they are targeted by lenders. Education alone, however, cannot counter marketing designed to make borrowing feel effortless. Regulators should therefore require rigorous affordability checks, clear disclosure of the total repayable amount and limits on excessive charges, and should bring newer forms of short-term credit under the same rules as conventional loans. Retailers could also be discouraged from presenting finance as the default option at checkout. Finally, free and impartial debt advice helps those already in difficulty to act before their situation worsens.

In conclusion, unaffordable credit can trap people in escalating debt, damage their wellbeing and weaken the wider economy. Financial education, combined with responsible lending rules, offers the most effective safeguard.
samples.why: Both parts sufficiently addressed with extended, well-supported ideas · prevention argued in stages, noting the limits of education · skilful cohesion · precise vocabulary (service existing debts, affordability checks) · error-free range of structures.
